text.p: Lehman Brothers slightly revised its earnings per share estimates (EPS) for Israel's Gilat Satellite Networks Ltd for the third and fourth quarters but maintained its outperform ranking for the company.

Lehman revised its estimate for the third quarter to $0.33 a share from $0.34 and for the fourth quarter to $0.41 from $0.40. Lehman left unchanged its full year estimate of $1.20 for 1996 and $1.54 for 1997.

"The rebalancing of our second half 1996 estimates reflects slightly higher marketing expenses in the third quarter of the year and improving sales growth forecast in the fourth quarter," Lehman said in a report.
Lehman estimated Gilat's revenues at $14.5 million in the third quarter and $17.5 million in the fourth quarter. It estimated full-year revenues of $53 million in 1996 and $70 million in 1997.

"Based on Gilat's strong competitive position in an exciting area of the expanding global telecommunications equipment market, we believe the company should continue to enjoy revenue growth of approximately 30 percent while increasing earnings by at least 25 to 30 percent in 1996 and 1997 and beyond," the report said.
Lehman set a 12-month price target of $26 for Gilat shares, which are currently trading at $18-1/2.
